english: Brother, do not tremble; do not tremble, sister. You, Fire, are awake, and the dog is awake (keeps watch). Let the night go away and the sun come. Then let the dew melt away. And may you live in the light. Sister, may you be content (at ease); do not tremble, sister. And now, brother, do not tremble.
uncertain: tréses / tréms: two different 'tremble' verbs (tréseti 'tremble in fear', trémti 'tremble'); mē + past (injunctive) read as prohibitive
léyteti: SBJV.3SG of léytt 'go away' (homonym 'touch' rejected)
tinéh₁eti: 'melt, thaw' vs 'stop, finish' (dew drying/ending)
tr̥pyéh₁s: OPT.2SG of térpt 'be sated/content' or trépt 'turn'; chose 'be content'
bʰéwdʰesi: PRS.2SG 'be awake' or SBJV.2SG of bʰéwdʰt 'wake up'
misfit: h₁n̥gʷnís: NOM.SG 'fire' as subject of 2SG bʰéwdʰesi; read as appositive 'you, Fire' (VOC h₁ń̥gʷni expected)

english: Fire, do not burn the man. And do not burn our lambs (rams). And do not burn our fence (enclosure). The fire was born in the water. Now, water, go. And go, water, to him (the fire). Water, cover him; the water is deep. May he (the man) grow strong, and may the grain increase.
uncertain: wr̥h₁énn̥s: 'lambs' or specifically 'rams'
wódr̥: read as VOC 'water' addressed throughout (alt. ACC goal 'go to the water', said to the fire)
tóm: masc. ACC 'him', taken as the fire each time; 'that water' would need neuter tód
h₃pusyéh₁t: 'increase', or 'may he become rich in grain' with ǵr̥h₂nóm as object
só: 'he' presumably the man protected by the charm

english: It is getting dark, and the wolf is creeping. Wolf, do not devour our sheep. And do not seize the lamb. The dog has seen you, and he is tracking you. Go away from us, lie down away from us. May our sheep live; may you not devour them. Whoever devours the lamb, may he vanish (perish). Wolf, go away!
uncertain: tód: neuter 'that/it' as dummy subject of 'is getting dark'
litdʰí: IMP of léytt 'go away' (homonym 'touch' rejected)
l̥gʰdʰí n̥sméd: 'lie down' with ablative 'from us' is odd; read 'lie down away from us'
n̥ḱyéh₁t: 'vanish, be lost' -> 'perish'

english: Fire, you are my brother. You know my word, and I am seeking offspring. Now give me offspring. Then may they live in the light (open space). May they grow strong; may they speak your name. Protect me, and protect my brother. I trust in you. Give me cattle (a cow), Fire, giver of good things.
uncertain: h₁idʰí: IMP of h₁áyt 'give' or h₁éyti 'go'; 'give' fits moy + gʷṓm
bʰh₂ih₁ént: OPT.3PL 'speak' (with h₁nómn̥ as object) vs homonym 'shine'
tóy: plural 'they' refers to singular collective ǵénh₁mn̥ 'offspring'
lowkóy: LOC of lowkós 'light space, clearing'
gʷṓm: 'a cow' or 'cattle' collectively

english: Dawn, daughter of the sky, I have seen you. You are red and you are great. When you come to us, the men awaken. Then the horses stood up. My parents sang to you. And you gave them imperishable fame. Give me cattle (a cow). Your garment is red. Do not leave me. And may I see you in the light.
uncertain: nos: 'to us' (with gʷm̥yési) or 'our' (with wiHrṓs 'our men')
bʰudʰént / sth₂ént: aorist 3PL after present 'when you come'; read as general 'awaken/stood up'
kh₂nónt: PST.3PL of kh₂néti; lexicon has no gloss, root keh₂n- 'sing'
h₁idʰí: 'give' (h₁áyt) vs 'go' (h₁éyti)
linékʷs: mē + past = 'do not leave'

english: Sun, I have seen your wheel. Dyeus set (placed) the wheel of the sun. When you came, Sun, the dew melted. Hear my song and watch over my cattle. And make my path straight. May my offspring live in your light. Sun, you are not mortal (dead). Now remember me.
uncertain: dʰéh₁t: 'put, placed' vs 'made, did'
spéḱye: 'keep looking at' -> 'watch over'
léwkesi: LOC of léwkos 'light' (alt. SBJV.2SG 'become bright' rejected)
néḱu: neuter form 'mortal/dead', agreeing with neuter sóh₂wl̥

english: Dawn, daughter of the sky, we speak to you. When you come, Dawn, the cattle stand up. Drive red cattle to us. And bring us strength and increase. Show us the path. Give us imperishable fame. Protect us with your light. I raise my song to you. We trust in you. May we know you; do not leave us.
uncertain: bʰh₂més: PRS.1PL 'speak' vs homonym bʰéh₂ti 'shine'
sth₂ént: aorist 3PL in a 'when' clause; read as general 'stand up'
nos (h₁rudʰróns nos gʷówn̥s): DAT 'to/for us' or GEN 'our red cattle'
woydéye: causative 'make see' -> 'show'
h₁idʰí: 'give' vs 'go'
ǵn̥h₃ih₁mé: OPT.1PL 'know' or 'get to know'

english: The rain-cloud came from the sky and rained on the grain. It (the grain) grew, and the springs filled. The gods saw the rain-cloud and they rejoiced. He who rained on the earth is Father Dyeus. He fills the springs and he fills the sea. Now may our cattle grow strong. Lead them to sweet water. May they drink and may they be sated.
uncertain: diwés: GEN/ABL; read ABL 'from the sky' (alt. 'the sky's rain-cloud')
ǵr̥h₂nóy: LOC 'on the grain' (alt. dual)
tód: neuter 'it', taken as the grain
wédʰe tóns swéh₂du wódr̥: 'lead them to sweet water' or 'bring them sweet water'
tr̥pih₁ént: OPT.3PL 'be sated' (térpt) vs 'turn' (trépt)

english: The priest said to the king: "Worship (sacrifice to) the god Werunos."
uncertain: ǵʰéwtōr: no gloss in lexicon; root ǵʰew- 'pour' -> 'pourer of libations, priest'
h₁yáǵeswo: MID.IMP.2SG of h₁yáǵeti (no gloss; root 'sacrifice/worship')
wérunom: not analyzed; taken as ACC of a god's name Werunos (cf. Varuna)
h₃rḗǵm̥: ACC addressee of 'said' -> 'said to the king'

english: The Sheep and the Horses
uncertain: owis, eḱwōses: not analyzed (older spelling without laryngeals); read as NOM.SG 'sheep' and NOM.PL 'horses'; a title

english: Father Dyeus, you are great. Dawn was born from you. The gods were born from you; the rain-cloud comes from you. Your name is famous. Now you listen to us. And you set the stars (in place). We bring you a sweet song. You are turned toward us. May we walk in your light.
uncertain: ḱléwsesi: PRS.2SG indicative 'you listen'; possibly meant as a request
dʰéh₁s: AOR.2SG 'you placed' (noun dʰéh₁s 'god' rejected)
ḱlutóm: neuter adjective 'famous' agreeing with h₁nómn̥ (verb reading rejected)
léwkesi: LOC 'in your light'

english: Who has seen Dawn? I have seen her, the daughter of the sky. She wears a red garment; she lifts up the light. Then she leads the sun. And come to us, Dawn! Bring us strength; bring us light. Now, Dawn, do not leave us. She is swift, and she is watchful. Dawn, you are not mortal.
uncertain: lowkóm: 'light space, clearing' -> 'the light'
sóh₂wl̥: NOM or ACC; read 'she leads the sun' (alt. 'the sun leads')
wédʰeti / wédʰe: 'lead, bring' (homonym 'bind, marry' rejected)
HHḱéwih₂: odd spelling with HH, read as feminine of HéHḱus 'swift'
n̥ḱéwih₂: feminine of néḱus 'dead/mortal' (zero-grade stem); read 'mortal'
misfit: h₂éwsōs: NOM.SG with IMP.2SG h₁r̥sḱé 'come'; VOC h₂éwsos expected for address

english: Dawn, the daughter of the sky, has arrived. Then the fire woke up. Fire, you are awake, and you warm us. You drive away distress; you are strong. We bring you a lamb, and you eat it. Now show us your light. We trust in you; you have come to love us. And may he remember us.
uncertain: h₂éǵesi: PRS.2SG 'drive' (alt. SBJV.2SG of h₂éǵt 'say')
h₂énǵʰos: 'narrowness' or 'anxiety, grief'
wénHs: AOR.2SG 'came to love, grew fond of'
só memn̥yéh₁t: 3rd person 'may he remember us', presumably the fire
misfit: só memn̥yéh₁t: shift to 3SG after addressing the fire in 2SG throughout; 2SG expected if the fire is meant

english: Father Dyeus, my cattle are thirsty. Now rain for me on the fields of my ancestors (parents). The springs filled and the sheep rejoiced. Now let it rain on my grain. Give water to my cattle. I bring you a song; listen to it. May I know you; now let me sing to you.
uncertain: h₂wérs: AOR.2SG or IMP.2SG of h₂wérst 'rain'; read as imperative
ǵn̥h₁trṓm: GEN.PL 'parents, begetters' -> 'ancestors'
pléh₁t / mudént: aorist, past; possibly meant as result
moy (ǵr̥h₂nóy): 'my grain' or 'for me'
kh₂nṓh₂: SBJV.1SG of kh₂néti; no gloss, root 'sing'

english: The Sheep and the Horses
uncertain: owis, eḱwōskʷe: not analyzed (older spelling without laryngeals, -kʷe written joined); read 'sheep' and 'horses' + 'and'; a title

english: Fire, I bring you a lamb. Now eat it. Carry my word to the gods. My parents gave you branches. Now I give you branches. Whoever gives to you, give him a cow. Give me imperishable fame. I trust in you. And may my fire not go out (vanish).
uncertain: h₁ddʰí: IMP 'eat' (two lexicon entries, same sense)
h₃ósdons: 'branches' or 'twigs' (firewood)
moy (péh₂wr̥): 'my fire' or 'for me'

english: Waters, you are mothers. You fill the sea, and it is deep. The water carries a load. The spring swells (becomes full). Bring us sweet water. And may you protect us. May we not thirst, Waters. Let us walk (climb) to you. Whoever drinks the water becomes joyful.
uncertain: h₁sté: PRS.2PL 'you are' (homonym h₁ést 'throw' rejected)
pl̥nh₁té / wédʰete: 2PL could be present or imperative; read pl̥nh₁té as statement, wédʰete as request
wos: ACC/DAT 'to you' as goal of 'walk'
méwdt: aorist in a general statement -> 'becomes joyful'

english: Dawn, daughter of the sky, you have shone forth (or: you are light). Then the night went away and the stars vanished. Carrying light, Dawn lit up the path. The sun follows her. She stretches out her wings (or: her wings spread out). Her light is sweet. Night is her sister. When you come to us, the men awaken. Dawn, show us the path. And remember our brothers. We sing your great fame.
uncertain: léwks: AOR.2SG of léwkt 'became bright' or NOM noun 'light'
n̥ḱént: 'vanished'
péth₂r̥h₂ tósyeh₂s tn̥néwti: neuter plural 'her wings/feathers' as subject or object of 3SG 'stretches'
lowkós: 'light space, clearing' -> 'light'
gʷéHyomes: no gloss; root geH- 'sing'
nos (bʰréh₂tern̥s): 'our brothers' or 'remember us, (our) brothers'

english: Sun, you light up the earth. Swift horses pull the wheel (chariot) of the sun. Hear me and remember me. Whoever speaks to you, give him light. May I see your light. And may my cattle not tremble. My brothers have seen (know) you. May my work succeed; I trust in you.
uncertain: kʷékʷlom: 'wheel' or 'chariot'
bʰéh₂ti: 'speaks' vs homonym 'shines'
widḗr: PRF.3PL 'have seen, know'
r̥h₁dʰyéh₁t: OPT.3SG 'carry out successfully'; subject unexpressed, read 'may my work succeed' (or 'may (he) accomplish my work')
lowkóm: 'light space' -> 'light'

english: The gods gave the sun a famous name. And they gave Dawn a famous name. The gods are givers of good things. Who knows the names of the gods? Now we know them. Gods, listen to us and protect us. The gods are not mortal. Let us go up (walk) to you. And may the gods not leave us.
uncertain: dʰh₁ént: 'placed, set' -> 'gave (a name)'
h₂uséy: DAT of h₂éwsōs 'Dawn' (or LOC of h₂ówsis 'at dawn')
ḱléwsete / h₂léksete: 2PL present or imperative; read as imperative
stéygʰōmes: SBJV.1PL 'let us walk/climb'

english: Dog, be awake! Guard our horses, dog. Kill the wolf; they (the horses) are lying down. And may he (the wolf) not come to us. And may he not see them. Whoever protects the horses, may the fire protect him. May they (the horses) thrive. Dog, be awake! Dog, guard our horses.
uncertain: tóy légʰyonti: 'they are lying down' (the horses) or 'those who are lying down'
n̥smé: ACC.PL 'us' (homonym AOR.1PL of nést rejected)
h₃pusih₁ént: 'increase, grow rich' -> 'thrive'
só: taken as the wolf

english: Father Dyeus, hear our word. You set (made) the springs. You slew the serpent, and the waters came forth. You are the giver of good things. You know us and you have come to love us. Now who gave us the rain-cloud? It is Dyeus. Then the earth drank the sweet water. We sing your famous name. Bring us strength and increase. Now remember us; may our work succeed.
uncertain: dʰéh₁s: AOR.2SG 'you placed/made' (noun 'god' rejected)
gʷʰéns: PST.2SG (imperfect) 'were slaying' -> 'slew'
h₁n̥dʰént: AOR.3PL 'came forth'
gʷéHyomes: no gloss; root 'sing'
r̥h₁dʰyéh₁t: subject unexpressed; 'may our work succeed'

english: Who set the wheel of the sun (in place)? Dyeus himself set it. Swift horses pull it. The gods have seen it. He is strong and he is swift. Now let us sing of the wheel of the sun. He is turned toward us; he is not mortal. And protect us with it.
uncertain: -ge: emphatic 'Dyeus himself / it was Dyeus'
só (ish₁rós, HéHḱus): 'he' Dyeus, or the wheel (masc. kʷékʷlos)
gʷéHyōmes: SBJV.1PL 'let us sing'
h₂lékse: IMP.2SG, addressee unstated (presumably Dyeus)
tóh₁: INS 'with it' (the wheel)

english: Mother Earth, you carry a burden. You carry us and you nourish us. The seed grew in the earth, and it grew strong. The rain-cloud rained, and you drank the sweet water. You are the mother of the gods; now listen to us. We suck at your breast. Give us flour and strength. May the field be productive.
uncertain: bʰoréyesi: 'carry around' -> 'carry'
h₂léh₁wr̥: 'something crushed' -> 'flour'
dʰugʰyéh₁t: OPT.3SG of dʰéwgʰti 'be productive' (vs dʰéwgʰt 'hit, meet')
péh₃s: AOR.2SG 'you drank', subject is Earth addressed

english: Now the fire lies in the branch (wood). A man seized the branch, and the fire came forth. Fire, you heat the water. It burns out of the branch. Now you cook the lamb. You are our brother, and you are our parent. We sat down by the fire and gave it a branch. Hearing our word, the fire blazed up (became bright). Now may it not go out.
uncertain: h₃ósdoy / h₃ósdom / h₃ósdōd: 'branch, twig' -> firewood
dʰégʷʰeti: 3SG with no stated subject; read 'it (the fire) burns'
h₁n̥gʷnéy: LOC 'by/at the fire'
tósmey: DAT 'to it/him' (the fire)
léwkt: AOR.3SG 'became bright' -> 'blazed up'
tód: neuter 'it' = péh₂wr̥

english: Dyeus and Earth are the parents of the gods. Dyeus is the father, and Earth is the mother. The gods were born from Sky and Earth. They are strong, and they are famous. Hear us, Father Dyeus, Mother Earth. They are watchful. Now give us increase. They have come to love us. And may our cattle increase.
uncertain: diwés ǵʰmés: GEN/ABL; read ABL 'born from Sky and Earth'
h₁opéyete: 2PL present or imperative; read as imperative
tóy (bʰebʰudʰḗr, wn̥Hént): 'they', probably the gods
ḱluté / h₁opéyete: 2PL addressed to the pair Dyeus and Earth; a dual would also be possible

english: Rain-cloud, you came from the sky and rained on the earth. The earth drank, and the springs filled. Then the sea filled with water. Whoever drinks your water rejoices. And bring water to us. May the seed increase, and may the gods rejoice. The rain-cloud is swift; now we sing to you.
uncertain: h₂wérs: AOR.2SG 'you rained' (also IMP)
wédn̥s: GEN 'filled with water'
méwdt: aorist in general statement -> 'rejoices'
gʷéHyomes: no gloss; root 'sing'

english: Earth, you nourish the sheep. Sweet dew lies on your field. The hedge is green. The sun warms the dew, and the grain grew. Who nourishes us? She nourishes us. She is the giver of good things. Whoever ploughs, he eats. Now may the seed grow strong. She has come to love us; now remember us.
uncertain: h₂életi nos: subject unexpressed, 'she (Earth)'
ǵʰelh₃wós: 'green' or 'yellow'
h₂wékst: AOR.3SG after present gʷʰr̥néwti; tense shift
séh₂: fem. 'she' (homonym IMP 'become sated' rejected)
memn̥dʰí: 2SG addressed to Earth after 3rd-person 'she'
misfit: déh₃tōr: masculine agent noun with feminine subject séh₂ (a feminine form would be expected)
